title: File each ticket's tags under the right ticket

blocks.text: The help desk's agents open tickets all day, each from a session of their own, and many tickets share a title such as `password reset`. Agents report that a ticket they just opened shows no tags, while a colleague's ticket opened at the same moment shows them, and that a new `password reset` ticket sometimes files its tags under one from last week.

`open(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/Tickets.java` inserts the ticket, then files the tags under the id it gets back. Write `insertTicket(connection, title)`: insert the ticket row and return the id the database gave that row. The id column is an identity column; the database chooses the value. About eight lines.

rows: a colleague's ticket is inserted while this one is being opened
the returned id is the "mailbox full" ticket, and it has both tags

cases.says: opening a ticket returns its id, and its tags are filed under that id
two tickets opened one after the other get different ids, each with its own tags
when another session inserts a ticket between this ticket's INSERT and the tags, the tags still go to this ticket
a ticket whose title an older ticket already has gets the new ticket's id, and the older one gets none of its tags

origin.section: The Database Assigns the Key; Ask the Statement That Inserted the Row

concepts: The generated key comes from getGeneratedKeys on the inserting statement, asked for at prepare time; SELECT MAX(id) can return another session's row.
